sentences.text:
2. The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 195 of 2023
(Session Trial No. 386 of 2025), under Sections 504, 506, 376 I.P.C., Police Station Kishanpur,
District Fatehpur, with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on bail.
3.  Learned counsel for the applicant argued that this is the second anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of applicant.
His first anticipatory bail was dismissed on merits vide order dated 14.08.2025 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 9433 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 9433 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Earlier, in the first anticipatory bail application a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order 24.09.2024 granted interim anticipatory bail to the applicant till the next date of listing, in compliance of such order the applicant before the concerned court and since then he is appearing regularly before the concerned trial court and he has not misused the interim anticipatory bail granted to him.
It has also been submitted that applicant has no criminal antecedents and the applicant undertakes to cooperate during the trial and he would appear as and when required by the concerned trial court.
It has been stated that in case, the applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate with the investigation and would obey all conditions of bail.

4. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the application for anticipatory bail by contending that the victim has adduced her evidence at the trial by making specific allegation of rape against the applicant, thus, applicant does not deserve any indulgence and the present second anticipatory bail application may be dismissed.
5.

From perusal of record it transpires that the victim (P.W.1) at the trial has made specific allegation of rape against the applicant as she alleged in her statements recorded under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., thus, she has supported the prosecution case at the trial.
6.

In the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. In the instant case, considering the settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail,

2 attending facts and circumstances of the case and considering the fact that applicant has failed to show any fresh ground for considering his second anticipatory bail application when his first anticipatory bail application has already been rejected on merits., without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, no case for anticipatory bail is made out.

entities.text: Amit Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In view of above, the present anticipatory bail application is rejected.

(Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.) November 4, 2025 Mustaqeem.
